_about: People, places and institutions. Every organisation and person here is fictional except the theorists, who are cited the way real wall texts cite them.

venues.name: Corderie
venues.description: The former rope factory: a 300-metre brick hall with two rows of thick brick columns, timber roof trusses and small high windows.
venues.light: grey daylight from small high windows mixed with track lighting

venues.name: Magazzini del Sale
venues.description: Fifteenth-century salt warehouses on the Zattere: long brick naves under heavy wooden beams, open towards the Giudecca canal.
venues.light: flat daylight through the open doors

venues.name: Central Pavilion
venues.description: A sequence of white galleries with skylights and grey linoleum floors, built and rebuilt since 1895.

venues.name: Palazzo Morosin, piano nobile
venues.description: The first floor of a sixteenth-century palazzo on the Grand Canal: terrazzo floors, faded stucco, tall windows, a Murano chandelier.
venues.light: soft side light from tall windows onto the canal

venues.name: Ex Chiesa di San Lio Nuovo
venues.description: A deconsecrated church in Castello: white plaster walls, side chapels, a marble floor with tomb slabs.
venues.floor: marble floor with old tomb slabs
venues.light: dim daylight from high windows and a few spotlights on a rail

venues.name: Squero Ex Cantieri Giudecca
venues.description: A former boatyard on Giudecca: a corrugated metal roof on steel trusses, a concrete slip running down to the water.
venues.light: hard daylight from the open side

venues.name: Giardino delle Vergini
venues.description: A walled garden behind the shipyard: gravel paths, plane trees, overgrown beds, a brick wall.

venues.name: Tese delle Nappe
venues.description: A long shed divided into black boxes for moving image works, each with a bench and a curtain.
venues.light: darkness, light only from the projection

venues.name: Armazém 16
venues.description: A dockside warehouse with a steel roof, painted columns and a view of the river.

venues.name: Palácio Sotto Mayor
venues.description: A nineteenth-century palace with azulejo panels, parquet floors and high ceilings.

venues.name: Galerias Municipais
venues.description: White municipal galleries with low ceilings and fluorescent tubes.

venues.name: Convento do Beato
venues.description: A former convent: vaulted white rooms, stone floors, a cloister with orange trees.

venues.name: Pepper House Warehouse
venues.description: A colonial-era spice warehouse: whitewashed brick, wooden rafters, a courtyard open to the harbour.

venues.name: Coir Factory
venues.description: A former coir factory: a long shed with a clay-tile roof on timber posts and a jetty on the water.
venues.light: daylight through gaps in the tiles

venues.name: Durbar Hall
venues.description: A renovated hall with white walls, ceiling fans and teak doors.

venues.name: La Halle aux Tabacs
venues.description: A former tobacco factory: a huge concrete hall, steel windows, painted lines on the floor.

venues.name: Fort Saint-Laurent
venues.description: Stone casemates in a seventeenth-century fort above the harbour.

venues.name: Musée des Docks
venues.description: White galleries with polished concrete floors in a converted dock building.

venues.name: Pier 1 Warehouse
venues.description: A harbour warehouse with a saw-tooth roof, shipping containers stacked outside.

venues.name: Museum of Contemporary Art, Eulsukdo
venues.description: Large white museum galleries with high ceilings.

venues.name: Former Bank Building, Jung-gu
venues.description: A 1930s bank hall with marble counters, a vault and tiled floors.
venues.light: mixed daylight and old pendant lamps
